lead: South Africa votes in local government elections today, with 29.2 million registered voters and polls open from 7am to 9pm. Overnight in the US, Democrats flipped North Carolina's Senate seat as midterm results came in.

items.title: South Africans head to the polls in local government elections today
items.summary: About 29.2 million registered voters can cast ballots at 23,696 stations from 7am to 9pm. Bring a smart ID, green barcoded ID book or temporary ID certificate, and vote where you are registered.

items.title: Over 1.4 million special votes cast, KZN second-highest
items.summary: Preliminary IEC figures show 1,425,942 people voted early over two days, about 451,000 of them through home visits. KwaZulu-Natal recorded 208,846 special votes, behind only Gauteng.

items.title: IEC condemns attempts to enter KZN election storage sites
items.summary: The commission says MK Party supporters tried to access voting-material warehouses, including one in eThekwini where police intervened, and sites in Richmond and Pietermaritzburg. It plans legal action against those involved.

items.title: MK Party regional organiser killed at his Umzumbe home
items.summary: Lastborn Shazi, an MK regional organiser on the KZN south coast, was shot dead on Monday. The party has called for calm and swift justice while police investigate.

items.title: GO!Durban C3 route between KwaMashu and Pinetown targeted for December
items.summary: eThekwini signed a process agreement with taxi and bus operators that will run services on the Bridge City to Pinetown corridor. Contracts and system testing must be completed before passengers can ride.

items.title: Joburg Water says supply system is at a critical stage
items.summary: Residents are asked to cut use by 15% after weekend outages and low pressure. The utility is throttling supply so reservoirs can recover and says fixing infrastructure will need over R30 billion.

items.title: Court sets aside National Lottery licence award to Sizekhaya
items.summary: The Pretoria High Court sent the decision back to Trade Minister Parks Tau to reconsider, suspending its order for two six-month periods. Ithuba, the reserve bidder, is studying the ruling.

items.title: Limpopo voter arrested for photographing his marked ballot
items.summary: A 32-year-old man was arrested after allegedly photographing his special-vote ballot in Lulekani; police are seeking a second man. The IEC reminds voters that photographing a marked ballot is prohibited.

items.title: Democrats flip North Carolina Senate seat in US midterms
items.summary: Fox News projected former governor Roy Cooper will beat Trump ally Michael Whatley for retiring Republican Thom Tillis's seat, boosting Democrats' push for the Senate. Counting continues across the country.

items.title: US strikes Iranian targets near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: US officials described them as defensive strikes after Iran fired at a US aircraft. Tehran says it could reopen Hormuz within two days if Washington lifts its blockade, and oil rose on the news.

items.title: Russian bombing of Ukrainian aid centre kills at least 26
items.summary: Guided bombs hit an aid distribution site and shelter in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, with about 20 people missing. Zelensky said the attack shows Russia does not want de-escalation.

items.title: US, Russia and Ukraine to hold talks in Abu Dhabi next week
items.summary: Delegations are due to meet on 10 and 11 November to discuss post-war security, de-escalation and humanitarian issues, while Zelensky warns of possible Russian strikes on energy targets.

items.title: Houthis advance to within 80km of Yemen's Aden
items.summary: It is the rebels' closest approach to the government's temporary seat since 2015, threatening the main Aden-Taiz road. The government has reshuffled its cabinet, naming three new ministers.

items.title: Ebola deaths pass 5,370 as DR Congo outbreak continues
items.summary: Africa CDC data show about 10,444 infections across DR Congo, Uganda and Kenya. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo strain, though trials are under way.

items.title: Rand softens and JSE slips ahead of election day
items.summary: The rand traded near R16.64 to the dollar on Tuesday, about 0.3% weaker, and the Top 40 fell about 0.7%. Analysts say the US decision to suspend SA from AGOA from January was largely priced in.

items.title: Diesel down by up to R1.20 a litre from today, petrol flat
items.summary: Petrol drops just 1c a litre, while paraffin rises R2.75 and LPG R1.83/kg. A fuel levy cut was largely offset by a new slate levy to recover a R15.9 billion shortfall.

items.title: Gold eases as US bond yields climb
items.summary: Gold fell on Tuesday as the US 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.97% and the dollar firmed slightly, with reports of softer jewellery demand in India.

items.title: PSG hit Villarreal for six; Bayern and Barcelona win in Champions League
items.summary: PSG won 6-0 in Spain, Bayern beat Atlético 2-0 in Madrid, Barcelona swept past Aston Villa 3-0 and Inter won 3-0 at Feyenoord on Tuesday.

items.title: Cunha double completes Man United comeback against Roma
items.summary: United came from behind to win 3-2 at Old Trafford, with Bruno Fernandes scoring a retaken penalty before Matheus Cunha struck twice.

items.title: Moerat returns as Boks prepare for Italy in Turin on Saturday
items.summary: Salmaan Moerat partners Ruan Nortje at lock in place of the injured Eben Etzebeth, with Siya Kolisi captaining a settled side in the Nations Championship.

items.title: Investigation finds 400-plus apps hiding abusive deepfake tools
items.summary: WIRED found a network of AI apps and sites, some disguised as harmless services and listed in major app stores. Apple removed 19 apps after being contacted.

items.title: New York Times and other publishers sue Brave over AI scraping
items.summary: The suit alleges Brave scraped journalism, bypassed paywalls and supplied content to AI companies. The claims have not yet been tested in court.
